title: SpaceX's Musk says Tesla merger good idea but far from certain, needs 50% of Tesla shares
body: The merger remark is likely to draw the most attention, particularly for Tesla shareholders, though Musk's own caveats suggest it is an idea rather than a plan, which may limit any sustained move. Requiring approval from half of all Tesla shares sets a high bar, so investors may treat the comment as a long-dated possibility rather than a near-term catalyst. The compute comments are a cleaner read-through: a claim that older Nvidia H100 chips now rent for more than when new points to tight supply across AI infrastructure, which would tend to support sentiment toward Nvidia, server makers and AI cloud providers. Coming on the same session as Super Micro's surprise upgrade, it adds to a run of strong AI demand signals. Musk floated a SpaceX-Tesla merger while stressing it may never happen, but his clearer message was that AI compute remains so scarce that even older chips are rising in value.

title: UBS flags 3 tests for the AI trade as Meta kicks off mega-cap tech earnings
body: With rates rising and financing costs higher, the tolerance for open-ended AI spending is narrowing, which puts capex guidance at the centre of market reaction this season. Any sign that spending is outpacing revenue could hit hyperscaler shares even on headline beats, while firm commitments to sustained investment would tend to support semiconductor and AI hardware names further up the supply chain. UBS's warning about company-specific volatility suggests results may produce sharper winners and losers than the broad AI trade has seen. Meta's report sets the early tone, as an advertising-led business funding heavy AI investment. title: Super Micro shares jump 14% as preliminary revenue tops forecast by about $4 billion
body: The update gives the AI hardware trade a fresh demand signal, and the after-hours moves in Dell and HPE show investors treating it as a read-through for the wider server group rather than a company-specific win. That matters given both stocks fell heavily last week, so the rebound may test whether that selling was overdone. The margin beat could carry more weight than the revenue figure, as it eases a long-running concern that Super Micro has had to trade profitability for volume. With limited detail until 3 November, the open question is customer concentration: how much of the surge comes from the large cloud providers versus newer AI-focused buyers, whose spending may be less durable. Super Micro did not just sell far more AI servers than expected, it kept more of the money from each one, and that combination briefly lifted the whole server sector.

title: Goldman Sachs says 6% nominal growth, not 5% yields, is what matters for small caps
body: The note offers a framework for holding small caps even if Treasury yields stay elevated, which could support rotation flows toward the segment as long as growth data hold up. The flip side is that the thesis is explicitly tied to nominal growth, so small caps may become more sensitive to economic data surprises than to moves in yields, with a softer PMI or GDP print a bigger threat than a rate rise. Goldman's view that inflation pressure is largely energy-driven also links the outlook to oil: a further spike in crude would test the argument that broader inflation is moderating. title: More from RBA's (hawkish) Hauser: Q3 trimmed mean set to run hotter than expected
body: Flagging a higher-than-expected trimmed mean a week before the official CPI release is an unusually direct steer, and it shifts the risk balance for 28 October toward an upside surprise. Combined with his view that capacity pressures are tighter than the RBA assumed, the remarks are likely to reinforce hike pricing for 3 November, which would tend to support the Australian dollar and lift short-end Australian yields. His comment on supply shocks matters for the oil channel: it suggests the RBA is less inclined to look through energy-driven price rises while expectations are at risk, making crude a more direct input into Australian rate pricing. Softer labour data gives the doves a counterweight, but Hauser's framing suggests it is not enough on its own to keep the Board on hold. --- RBA 2026 dates, next meeting in just a couple of weeks time: - Hauser has all but previewed a hot underlying inflation print, and with capacity tighter than assumed and supply shocks no longer something to look through, a softer jobs market looks like a footnote rather than a reprieve.

title: BOJ seen lifting rates to 1.50% in December as 69% of economists expect a Q4 hike
body: The poll firms up December as the likely window for the BOJ's next move, which should limit yen sensitivity to the 30 October meeting but raises the stakes around the December decision. The bigger currency risk may be the vote itself: with the yen only modestly above its 2026 low, a repeat of September's dissent from government-nominated board members could be read as political resistance to tightening and trigger fresh selling. Rising energy and import costs tied to the Middle East war keep oil a direct input into Japan's inflation outlook, so a further jump in crude would likely harden the case for hikes. For JGBs, the shift toward a 2% or higher terminal rate, combined with fiscal concerns, points to continued pressure on yields. - Economists now broadly expect the BOJ to keep raising rates every quarter, with the main risk to the yen coming not from the timing of the next move but from who votes against it.

body: Crude oil stabilized near $98 per barrel on Wednesday after sharp swings in the previous session, as investors weighed conflicting signals over diplomatic progress between the US and Iran. Prices had slumped on Tuesday following a visit by Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, to Tehran, where he met senior Iranian diplomatic and military officials to discuss bilateral relations and the status of talks with Washington. However, a diplomat involved in the negotiations rejected reports that an agreement was imminent, while confirming that efforts to resolve the conflict are ongoing. Oil prices are up more than 10% this month, driven by mounting supply concerns amid escalating hostilities involving Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi forces, as well as the continuing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. At least 18 vessels have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks. Despite these disruptions, crude shipments from the Middle East have largely rebounded and are now estimated at around 80% of prewar levels. title: NEXTDC shares plunge 44% as power delays expose AI data centre bottleneck
body: NEXTDC's downgrade is a stark example of a risk investors have tended to treat as theoretical: that grid access and local opposition, not customer demand, cap how fast data centre capacity can be built. The read-through extends well beyond Australia, as operators and AI cloud providers globally depend on utilities and planning authorities that move more slowly than hyperscaler spending plans. It echoes the warning in Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus, reported this week, that resistance to data centres is becoming more organised across jurisdictions. Investors may now apply a larger discount to contracted-but-undelivered capacity across the sector, particularly where projects depend on new grid connections. - NEXTDC had the customers and the contracts, but not the electricity, and its 44% share collapse shows the AI build-out now runs only as fast as the local grid and the local council allow.

title: Nvidia in talks to invest hundreds of millions in Firmus after AI cloud firm's IPO flop
body: A fresh Nvidia investment would reassure holders of neocloud debt and equity that the sector's largest supplier remains willing to support it, even as public markets turn more selective. The flip side is that Nvidia backing companies that buy its chips may sharpen questions about how much AI infrastructure demand depends on vendor financing rather than independent capital, an issue that sits at the heart of the bubble debate Ken Griffin revived on Tuesday. For Nvidia shares, the amounts involved are small, so the signal matters more than the money. The episode also suggests the IPO window for AI infrastructure firms is narrowing, pushing more of them toward private and strategic funding. - When public investors walked away from Firmus, Nvidia appears ready to step in, a reminder that the AI cloud boom still leans heavily on its biggest supplier.

The energy channel is the one to watch: Russia's diesel supply deal with Washington and the pause in new US sanctions were aimed partly at keeping Moscow out of the war with Iran, so any rupture in that arrangement could tighten fuel markets already strained by the Middle East conflict. Drone strikes on commercial ships in the Black Sea add a shipping risk premium near NATO waters. The narrowing deficit owes much to oil disruption rather than weaker demand: Houthi rerouting delayed crude arrivals, so the import bill is likely to rebound in October as Suez-routed tankers arrive and procurement returns to around year-earlier levels. That makes oil prices and Middle East shipping the key swing factor for Japan's trade balance and the yen's import-driven pressure in the months ahead. For the BOJ, solid external demand adds to the case for a December hike, with its 30 October meeting and fresh forecasts the next focus. Japan's exporters are still riding the AI boom, but September's narrower trade gap owes more to delayed oil tankers than to any lasting improvement.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6779 – Reuters estimate
body: The fixing mechanism matters most right now because its message has shifted over the past month. For nearly a year, the PBOC has set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, which traders read as an effort to slow the yuan's appreciation, and in late August that gap reached its widest since February, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high. Through October, however, the midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the central bank has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The fixing is still set weaker than models imply, so this looks like a loosening of the brakes rather than their removal. The balance Beijing is weighing is unchanged: a firmer currency supports capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness while the domestic economy remains soft. The gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest guides to how far the PBOC is willing to let the yuan run.--- The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and after months of saying slow down, it has lately been saying go, gradually.Summary: The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets.

title: Citadel's Griffin says AI "almost certainly" a bubble, even as demand signals stay strong
body: A bubble call from one of the most closely watched figures in finance is likely to sharpen the debate over AI valuations, though Griffin's framing stops well short of a call to exit. His argument that transformative shifts usually come with a bubble implies volatility and losers along the way, not a collapse in the underlying trend, which may limit any direct market reaction. The timing is notable: his comments arrived alongside SpaceX's AI revenue beat, Super Micro's surprise upgrade and Musk's claim that compute remains scarce, so investors are weighing strong near-term demand against concerns about how much of it is already priced in. That tension may feed the stock-specific volatility analysts expect this earnings season. Griffin thinks AI is both a bubble and the real thing, which is less a contradiction than a reminder that the dot-com bust still left Amazon standing.

title: Rupee Hits 6-Week High on IPO Inflows
body: The Indian rupee traded near 94.6 per dollar, touching a six-week high after the holiday, supported by anticipated dollar inflows from Jio Platforms' IPO and continued intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The currency extended its winning streak to a seventh consecutive session and is now up 5.18% year-to-date, as the central bank persisted with dollar sales and intensified scrutiny of large overseas investments to stem capital outflows. Investors are now awaiting the release of the RBI's October policy meeting minutes later on Wednesday for signals on the likelihood of further rate hikes, following the recent 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate to 5.50%. Nonetheless, elevated oil prices continue to pose a downside risk, as higher crude costs could widen India's import bill and bolster demand for dollars. title: Palm Oil Nears MYR 4,800 as Profit-Taking Offsets Demand
body: Malaysian palm oil futures slipped towards MYR 4,800 per tonne as traders booked profits after prices neared a four‑week high. Sentiment was further pressured by record inventories of 3.51 million tonnes in September, with seasonal output expected to remain strong in October following six straight months of increases. However, the downside was limited by firmer edible oil prices on the Dalian and Chicago exchanges. Export activity also provided support, as cargo surveyors reported a 43.2%–58.3% month‑on‑month jump in palm oil shipments during the first half of October. Festival‑driven demand from India, a major buyer, helped bolster risk appetite. At the same time, Indonesia raised its October crude palm oil reference price to USD 1,042.15 per tonne, while higher crude oil prices improved palm oil's appeal as a biodiesel feedstock. Traders are now closely watching Malaysia's potential move to waive or cut its crude palm oil export tax, a step that could strengthen the country's competitiveness against Indonesian supplies. title: US 10-Year Yield Steadies on Inflation Worries
body: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note held near 5.12% on Wednesday, stabilizing after the previous session's pullback, as rising oil prices reignited inflation worries and reinforced expectations of further interest rate hikes. Crude prices resumed their upward trend after a diplomat dismissed reports that a deal to resolve tensions between the US and Iran was imminent, while confirming that talks are still in progress. At the same time, the US Federal Reserve is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at next week's meeting, though markets are still pricing in the possibility of a rate increase in December. Treasury yields had already climbed to multi-decade highs earlier this month amid a global bond selloff, driven by persistent energy-related inflation, growing government debt burdens, and worsening fiscal conditions in major economies. title: Rupiah Holds Gains as BI Rate Decision Looms
body: The Indonesian rupiah hovered near IDR 17,970 per dollar on Wednesday, extending its advance for a third straight session as the US dollar stayed under pressure after the dollar index slipped to a three-week low. Softer US Treasury yields and easing crude oil prices reduced support for the greenback, bolstering emerging market currencies, including the rupiah. Investors were focused on Bank Indonesia's policy decision due later in the day, with markets widely expecting the central bank to keep its benchmark rate unchanged at 5.75% for a fourth consecutive month, following a cumulative 100 basis points of tightening earlier this year. Sentiment was further supported by fading worries that MSCI might reclassify Indonesia as a standalone market, after regulators rolled out measures to tackle concentrated share ownership and tighten shareholder disclosure rules. Still, the rupiah's gains were capped by lingering risks from elevated oil prices, which could pressure the fiscal position, and mounting inflationary concerns tied to El Niño-related increases in food costs. title: Yen Holds Steady Amid Sluggish Export Growth
body: The Japanese yen was steady around 158.2 per dollar on Wednesday, trading in a tight range as investors digested data showing that September exports rose less than expected and registered their weakest growth since April. Even so, exports extended their winning streak to a 13th consecutive month, underpinned by solid demand for semiconductors and AI-related products. On the policy front, the Bank of Japan is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at next week's meeting, with markets looking for a possible rate hike in December. Earlier this week, Governor Kazuo Ueda indicated that underlying inflation is approaching the BOJ's 2% target, bolstering expectations for a more hawkish tilt. However, the yen remains under pressure from ongoing carry trades, as Japan's comparatively low interest rates continue to erode its appeal. The BOJ's gradual pace of tightening is also seen as insufficient to significantly narrow the interest rate gap with other major economies. title: US Natgas Prices Edge Higher
body: US natural gas prices inched up to $2.97 per MMBtu on Wednesday, attempting to recover from a four-week low seen in the prior session, as stronger LNG export activity and lower production partially offset soft demand amid mild weather conditions. Average gas flows to the nine major US LNG export terminals have increased to 18.2 bcfd so far in October, up from 17.9 bcfd in September. At the same time, gas output in the Lower 48 states has averaged 111.4 bcfd this month, down from the record 113.3 bcfd reached in both August and September. The storage surplus continued to narrow as well, with inventories as of October 9 standing 3.9% below year-ago levels and just 1.3% above the five-year average. Looking ahead, mild temperatures are expected to persist through late October, restraining both heating and cooling demand, while forecasts for a "Super El Niño" are further dampening the winter demand outlook. title: Indonesian Shares Retreat Ahead of BI Rate Call
body: Indonesian equities dropped 84 points, or 1.6%, to 5,197 on Wednesday morning, erasing earlier gains that followed new regulatory steps aimed at restoring investor confidence. The measures included adjustments to stocks with highly concentrated ownership and enhanced disclosure requirements for shareholder affiliations. Sentiment turned cautious ahead of Bank Indonesia's policy decision later in the day. The central bank is widely expected to keep its benchmark rate unchanged for a fourth consecutive month, but scope for further easing remains limited after a cumulative 100-basis-point hike in May and June. Losses were partially contained by record foreign direct investment in Q3 2026, underpinned by strong inflows into the base metal sector. Externally, China—Indonesia's key trading partner—left its benchmark lending rates steady for a 17th straight month, following stronger-than-expected Q3 GDP data. Sector-wise, cyclicals, basic materials, and financials led the declines, while infrastructure, non-cyclicals, and transport provided some support. title: Taiwan Stocks Rebound from Near 5-Week Low
body: The TAIEX, Taiwan's benchmark stock index, rose 860 points, or 1.9%, to 47,153 in Wednesday morning trading, fully reversing losses from the previous two sessions. The advance followed overnight gains on Wall Street, supported by easing US Treasury yields and lower oil prices. The broader market pulled away from its lowest level since September 17, hit just a day earlier, with the recovery led primarily by electronic technology and financial stocks. Electronic technology shares rebounded, climbing 1.5% after a 1.0% decline in the prior session driven by worries over AI-related investment. Softer oil prices helped improve risk sentiment, alleviating concerns about inflationary pressures and further interest rate hikes. TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker and a heavyweight accounting for more than 40% of the Taiwan market's total capitalization, advanced 1.0%. Among other major tech names, MediaTek, Delta Electronics, and Hon Hai Precision gained 2.2%, 2.8%, and 2.5%, respectively. The financial sector also staged a recovery, adding 1.1%, supported mainly by Fubon Financial, up 0.7%, and Cathay Financial, which climbed 2.5%. title: European Natural Gas Rebounds
body: European natural gas prices climbed to €87 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, rebounding toward multi‑year highs after falling more than 3% in the previous session, as traders digested conflicting signals over diplomatic efforts to end the war in the Middle East. Tuesday's pullback had been driven by unconfirmed reports that Qatar and Pakistan had put forward a new proposal to revive peace talks. However, a diplomat involved in the negotiations later said that speculation about an imminent agreement was inaccurate. Even after the brief decline, European gas prices remain more than twice their pre‑war levels, reflecting continuing disruptions to LNG shipments from the Persian Gulf and unusually low stockpiles. As of October 20, European gas storage sites were 74.62% full, the lowest level for this time of year since records began in 2009. The situation is especially worrying in Germany, the region's largest economy, where storage levels are only just above 61%. Strong LNG demand from Asia further heightens the risk of fiercer competition for cargoes as colder weather sets in. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Heating Oil Moves Toward Record
body: US heating oil futures climbed to about $5 per gallon, approaching the record high reached in mid-September, after industry data pointed to a drawdown in inventories. API figures indicated that US distillate stocks fell by 2.6 million barrels in the week ending October 16, highlighting persistently tight supply conditions. Supply concerns were further amplified by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Attacks on oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz intensified fears of shipping disruptions, while Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure stoked worries over additional supply losses. Even so, Gulf oil shipments proved more resilient than many had anticipated, with exports surpassing pre-war levels in mid-October. At the same time, traders continued to assess the potential impact of increased Russian fuel exports after President Trump waived newly imposed Russia-related sanctions and tariffs. Secretary of State Marco Rubio noted that the administration could take up to 60 days to evaluate their economic effects, leaving markets uncertain over whether the policy shift would ultimately ease fuel supply pressures. title: AUS 10Y Yield Trades Near Multi-Week Lows
body: Australia's 10-year government bond yield hovered around 5.2%, near multi-week lows, as investors continued to reassess the monetary policy outlook. RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said tighter policy was having an impact, but warned that the inflation outlook remained "materially worse," in part because of elevated oil prices. He emphasized the importance of keeping inflation expectations anchored ahead of the RBA's November 3 policy meeting, at which officials will decide whether to raise interest rates for a fifth time this year. At the same time, Hauser acknowledged that higher borrowing costs and fuel prices were weighing on economic activity. Following his remarks, markets increased the implied probability of a November rate hike to 44%, up from 30% at the start of the week, while the likelihood of a December move rose to 64%. Attention now turns to next week's third-quarter inflation report. Core inflation is forecast to climb 1.0% quarter-on-quarter, from 0.9% previously, leaving the annual rate at 3.5%—still well above the RBA's target range. title: China Youth Jobless Rate Eases to 18%
body: China's urban youth unemployment rate for 16–24-year-olds, excluding students, eased to 18% in September 2026, down from 18.9% in August, when it hit a 12-month high. The National Bureau of Statistics attributed the month-on-month decline to new graduates gradually finding jobs following the seasonal spike in unemployment during the July–August graduation period. The jobless rate for 25–29-year-olds in cities edged down to 7.4% from 7.5%, while the rate for those aged 30–59 held steady at 3.9%. Overall, the nationwide urban unemployment rate dipped to 5.2% from 5.3%, signaling a modest improvement in labor market conditions. title: Japan Trade Gap Widens Sharply
body: Japan's trade deficit widened sharply to JPY 536.6 billion in September 2026, up from JPY 277.7 billion a year earlier, surpassing market expectations of a JPY 181.0 billion shortfall and marking the fifth consecutive monthly deficit. The deterioration reflected import growth outpacing that of exports. Imports climbed 18.9% year-on-year to JPY 11,508.8 billion, slowing from August's 28.0% surge and coming in below the forecast 19.6%, the weakest increase since May. Nevertheless, crude oil imports soared 51.1%, partly due to Japan's efforts to diversify energy sources amid heightened tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Exports rose 16.7% to JPY 10,972.2 billion, undershooting estimates of 20.1% and signaling the slowest growth in five months, though shipments still extended their expansion streak to 13 months. Robust demand for AI-related semiconductors continued to underpin exports, while supply-chain disruptions tied to the Middle East conflict acted as a drag.
